args.reason: The supersession argument is unsound. The old decision is a security rule: secrets come from environment variables only and are never written to .faff/. The new decision writes resolved API keys in plain text to .faff/cache/credentials.json, which directly breaks that rule. Gitignore only keeps the file out of commits; the key still sits on disk where logs, backups, sandbox copies, artifact uploads, or any process reading .faff/ can pick it up, and it outlives the session and any key rotation. The stated benefit is also weak: process.env is an in-memory lookup, so its cost per LLM call is negligible next to a network round trip, and an in-process variable would give the same caching with no file. The argument never addresses why the original rule existed, so it has not shown that the old rationale no longer holds.
